facts.content: Patient has a 3-day history of watery diarrhea occurring approximately 6 to 7 times per day.
Patient experiences left lower quadrant crampy intermittent abdominal pain.
Patient had one episode of vomiting at onset, which has now resolved.
facts.source_text: 1 episode vomiting at onset, now resolved

facts.content: Subjective fever on day 1 and feels weak and shaky.
Appetite has decreased; patient tolerates soups, smoothies, and fluids.
Symptoms were triggered by eating Chinese takeaway 4 days ago; one child also vomited.
facts.source_text: Trigger: Chinese takeaway 4 days ago; one child vomited only

facts.content: Patient is an accountant living with wife and two kids.
facts.source_text: SH: Accountant; lives w/ wife + 2 kids

facts.content: Patient does not smoke and does not consume alcohol.
Assessment is acute gastroenteritis likely viral or food-borne.
Encourage oral rehydration with fluids and over-the-counter oral rehydration solutions like Dioralyte.
facts.source_text: Oral rehydration: encourage fluids + OTC ORS (e.g., Dioralyte)

facts.content: Take Paracetamol 1 g orally every 6 hours as needed for fever or pain, with a maximum of 4 g in 24 hours.
facts.source_text: Paracetamol 1 g PO q6h PRN fever/pain (max 4 g/24 h)

facts.content: Patient advised to rest and take 2 to 3 days off work.
Return to clinic or seek care if no improvement by 3 to 4 days, increased abdominal pain, blood in stool, persistent vomiting, or fever greater than 38°C.
facts.source_text: RTC/seek care if no improvement ≥3–4 days, ↑abd pain, blood in stool, persistent vomiting, fever >38 °C

facts.content: Consider stool culture and labs if symptoms persist.
facts.source_text: Consider stool culture, labs if symptoms persist

facts.content: Continue using usual inhaler for asthma.
